note: Hand-written form tips. Ids listed here are never pruned by tools/build_library.py. Exactly three strings per id, each at most 90 characters, no placeholders.

bench-press: Retract your shoulder blades and keep them pinned to the bench.
Lower the bar to mid-chest with your elbows at about 45 degrees.
Drive your feet into the floor and press the bar over your shoulders.
incline-bench-press: Set the bench near 30 degrees so your front delts do not take over.
Lower the bar to your upper chest and keep your wrists stacked.
Press up and slightly back; do not let your shoulders roll forward.
dumbbell-bench-press: Set your shoulder blades first, then kick the dumbbells into place.
Lower until your upper arms are level with your torso, no deeper.
Press up and slightly in; stop before the dumbbells clang together.
machine-chest-press: Set the handles level with your mid-chest before the first rep.
Keep your back and head against the pad through the whole press.
Press smoothly and stop just short of locking out your elbows.
push-up: Hands just outside shoulder width, body in one straight line.
Lower until your chest is a fist off the floor, elbows at 45 degrees.
Push the floor away and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag.
dip: Start at the top with your shoulders pulled down, not shrugged.
Lower until your upper arms reach parallel; lean forward for chest.
Stop the set if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
cable-fly: Set the pulleys at chest height and take a small step forward.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows and hug your arms together.
Let your arms travel back only until you feel a stretch across the chest.
overhead-press: Start with the bar at collarbone height, ribs down, glutes tight.
Press straight up and move your head slightly back and through.
Finish with your biceps by your ears; do not arch your lower back.
seated-dumbbell-press: Sit tall against the pad with the dumbbells at ear height.
Press up until your arms are straight, keeping your ribs down.
Lower under control back to ear height; do not bounce out of the bottom.
lateral-raise: Stand tall with a slight bend in your elbows and your thumbs level.
Raise out to the sides only until your hands reach shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows and lower over two seconds; no swinging.
rear-delt-fly: Hinge forward with a flat back and let your arms hang straight down.
Pull your arms out to the sides, leading with your little fingers.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together without shrugging your traps.
face-pull: Set the rope at eye level and step back until your arms are straight.
Pull the rope toward your forehead and spread your hands apart.
Finish with your elbows high and your shoulder blades pulled back.
pull-up: Start from a dead hang with your shoulders active, not slack.
Drive your elbows down to your ribs and lead with your chest.
Lower all the way to a straight-arm hang; no kipping or swinging.
chin-up: Grip the bar palms facing you, hands about shoulder width apart.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, keeping your elbows in front.
Lower slowly to a full hang; stop the set once you start swinging.
lat-pulldown: Grip slightly wider than your shoulders and pin your thighs down.
Pull the bar to your upper chest by driving your elbows down.
Let the bar rise until your arms are straight; do not lean back to pull.
barbell-row: Hinge to about 45 degrees with a flat back and the bar hanging.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs by driving your elbows back.
Lower under control and keep your torso still, with no jerking upright.
one-arm-dumbbell-row: Support one hand and knee on the bench with a flat, square back.
Pull the dumbbell to your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Lower until your arm is straight and your shoulder blade reaches forward.
seated-row: Sit tall with a slight knee bend and your chest lifted.
Pull the handle to your belly button, elbows passing your ribs.
Let your shoulder blades travel forward on the return; do not round.
chest-supported-row: Rest your chest on the pad and let your arms hang straight down.
Row with your elbows until the handles touch the pad by your ribs.
Lower fully until your shoulder blades reach forward; do not shrug.
t-bar-row: Straddle the bar with a flat back and your chest lifted.
Pull the handles to your chest with your elbows tracking back.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly without dropping your chest.
deadlift: Set the bar over mid-foot with your shins almost touching it.
Brace hard, then push the floor away with a flat back and straight arms.
Stand tall by squeezing your glutes; do not lean back at the top.
romanian-deadlift: Start standing with soft knees and the bar against your thighs.
Push your hips back and let the bar slide down your legs.
Stop at a hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand.
sumo-deadlift: Take a wide stance, toes turned out, with your shins vertical.
Grip inside your knees, brace, and push the floor apart.
Keep the bar close and finish with your glutes, not by leaning back.
hip-thrust: Rest your upper back on the bench, feet flat and shoulder width.
Drive through your heels until your hips are level with your knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top; do not overarch your lower back.
barbell-glute-bridge: Lie on the floor with the bar over your hips and feet planted.
Tuck your pelvis slightly, then lift your hips with your glutes.
Stop when your body is a straight line from knees to shoulders.
back-extension: Set the pad just below your hip bones and cross your arms.
Lower until you feel a stretch, then rise until your body is straight.
Stop at a straight line and squeeze your glutes; do not hyperextend.
good-morning: Rest the bar on your upper back with a small bend in your knees.
Push your hips back and lower your torso until it is near parallel.
Keep your back flat and rise by driving your hips forward.
squat: Brace your core and set the bar on your upper back before stepping out.
Sit down and back until your hip crease drops below your knee.
Drive through mid-foot and keep your knees tracking over your toes.
front-squat: Rest the bar on your front delts with your elbows held high.
Stay upright and sit straight down, keeping your elbows up.
Drive up through your whole foot without letting your chest drop.
goblet-squat: Hold one dumbbell at your chest with your elbows tucked in.
Sit down between your feet, chest tall and heels flat on the floor.
Drive up through your heels and finish with your glutes squeezed.
leg-press: Set your feet shoulder width on the platform, toes slightly out.
Lower until your knees reach 90 degrees; keep your back on the pad.
Press through your whole foot without locking your knees at the top.
hack-squat: Set your shoulders under the pads with your back flat on the sled.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel, knees over your toes.
Drive through mid-foot and stop just short of locking out.
smith-machine-squat: Place your feet slightly forward of the bar with your back flat.
Lower under control until your thighs reach parallel.
Push through your heels and keep the bar path straight.
bulgarian-split-squat: Rest the top of your back foot on a bench, front foot a step ahead.
Lower straight down until your back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright and push through your front heel to stand.
walking-lunge: Step forward far enough that your front shin stays near vertical.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor.
Push off the front heel and step straight into the next lunge.
reverse-lunge: Step back and keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor, torso upright.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
leg-extension: Line your knee up with the machine pivot and hold the handles.
Straighten your legs fully and pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly; do not let the stack drop or swing the weight.
seated-leg-curl: Set the pad just above your heels and keep your back on the seat.
Curl your heels down and under, squeezing your hamstrings.
Return slowly until your legs are almost straight; keep your hips down.
standing-calf-raise: Stand with the balls of your feet on the platform, knees straight.
Rise as high as you can and pause for a second at the top.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your calf, then repeat.
seated-calf-raise: Sit with the pad on your thighs and the balls of your feet supported.
Push up as high as you can, then pause and squeeze your calves.
Lower slowly until you feel a deep stretch in your calf.
ez-bar-curl: Stand tall with your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the bar up without swinging your torso or shoulders.
Lower over two seconds until your arms are straight.
hammer-curl: Hold the dumbbells with your palms facing each other.
Curl straight up, keeping your elbows tight to your ribs.
Lower slowly and end the set once you start to swing.
skull-crusher: Lie down with the bar over your forehead and elbows pointing up.
Bend only at the elbows and lower the bar toward your hairline.
Press back up without letting your elbows drift toward your feet.
tricep-pushdown: Stand close to the cable with your elbows pinned to your sides.
Push the handle down until your arms are straight, then squeeze.
Let the handle rise only until your forearms reach horizontal.
farmer-carry: Stand tall between the dumbbells with your shoulders pulled back.
Grip hard, brace your core, and walk with short, even steps.
Keep your ribs down and do not let your torso lean to one side.
plank: Set your elbows under your shoulders and your feet hip width.
Brace as if you were about to be punched in the stomach.
Keep a straight line from shoulders to heels; do not let your hips sag.
hanging-leg-raise: Hang with your shoulders active and your legs held together.
Raise your legs without swinging and curl your pelvis up at the top.
Lower slowly to a full hang and stop before you start to swing.
cat-cow-stretch: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders.
Round your spine as you breathe out, then let it sag as you breathe in.
Move slowly through the whole range; never force the end position.
arm-circles: Stand tall with your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Draw small circles first, then gradually make them larger.
Reverse the direction halfway through the set.
worlds-greatest-stretch: Step into a deep lunge and place both hands inside your front foot.
Drop your back knee, then rotate your chest toward your front leg.
Reach the top arm to the ceiling and breathe out as you settle.
leg-swings-stretch: Hold a wall for balance and keep your torso upright.
Swing one leg forward and back in a smooth, controlled arc.
Keep the range pain-free and switch legs halfway through.
torso-twist-stretch: Stand with your feet hip width and your knees soft.
Rotate your ribcage to one side, letting your arms swing freely.
Keep your hips fairly still and do not force the end of the range.
childs-pose: Kneel with your big toes together and your knees apart.
Sit back onto your heels and walk your hands forward.
Let your chest sink toward the floor and breathe into your back.
kneeling-hip-flexor-stretch: Kneel on one knee with the other foot planted in front.
Tuck your pelvis under and squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Push your hips gently forward until the front of the hip opens.
hamstring-stretch: Sit with one leg straight and the other foot tucked in.
Hinge from your hips with a flat back toward the straight leg.
Stop at a gentle stretch; do not round your back to reach further.
standing-quad-stretch: Stand tall and hold a wall with one hand for balance.
Pull your heel toward your glute and keep your knees together.
Tuck your pelvis under so the stretch stays in the front of the thigh.
seated-forward-fold-stretch: Sit with both legs straight and your feet flexed.
Hinge forward from your hips, keeping your back as flat as you can.
Hold where you feel a gentle hamstring stretch, not pain.
cross-body-shoulder-stretch: Bring one arm across your chest at shoulder height.
Hook your other arm above the elbow and pull gently inward.
Keep your shoulder down; do not let it roll forward.
wall-calf-stretch: Place your hands on a wall with one leg back and heel down.
Keep the back knee straight and lean your hips forward.
Hold the stretch and breathe; switch legs halfway through.
butterfly-stretch: Sit with the soles of your feet together and your knees out.
Hold your feet and sit tall with a long spine.
Let your knees drop with gravity; do not press them down.
